# `positions_transition`

a surface's positions brought into another coordinate system of its space by its transition operator.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run positions_transition --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run positions_transition --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run positions_transition --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex --transition T1_mni --name cortex_mni
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `surface` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$surface"} | yes |
| `transition` | operator transition, where {"name": "$transition"} | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `surface` | `--surface` | none | - |  | the surface by name |
| `transition` | `--transition` | none | - |  | the transition operator by name (kind transition) |
| `name` | `--name` | `{surface}_{transition}` | - |  | the new surface's name |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`meeg.positions_transition`](../nodes.md) | positions=surface, transition=transition |  | moved |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `moved` | kind manifold, type surface, name $name, derived_from surface.manifold.0 |

## Notes from the definition

```text
A SURFACE'S POSITIONS IN ANOTHER COORDINATE SYSTEM OF ITS SPACE (a new surface): its vertices through an operator of kind transition (an affine of the space's two systems:
SCS to MNI, voxel to SCS, ...). The checker never applies a transition itself: when two inputs' systems differ it names this pipeline. The faces are kept.

  nxr-neuro run positions_transition --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex --transition T1_mni --name cortex_mni
```
